summary: Adaptive retention policy causes missing series in filtered dashboard time-series
description:
Issue summary: After the new adaptive retention rollout, several FluxHealth dashboards show entire time-series missing when a custom time-range + tag filter is applied. The graphs appear to have zero datapoints for specific series that previously existed. This seems correlated with the adaptive retention compaction job (v2) that ran during the customer-specified retention window.

Impact: Data loss perception to customer; multiple SLA alerts fired for missing metrics. Affects 4 business-critical dashboards used by FluxHealth ops: API latency, ingestion-rate, cost-by-route, and tracehook-errors. Customer reporting inability to reconcile usage to billing for a 6-hour window.

Environment: prod (us-east-1), customer org: FluxHealth (enterprise), dashboards served from console cluster console-prod-3. Adaptive retention rollout v2 started 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC.

Observed behavior: When applying a dashboard-level tag filter (route: /v1/generate) and time-range that crosses the retention boundary (example 2026-03-08 20:00 to 2026-03-09 05:00), one or more series within panels return no datapoints. Other series remain intact. Exported CSV for panel returns header rows with metrics but empty numeric values for missing series.

Expected behavior: Series should either show aggregated/rollup values or indicate sparse data but not drop entire series from the time-series output.

Steps to reproduce: See steps_to_reproduce field for operator checklist.

Notes: This ticket created by CS after customer-provided screenshots and CSVs. Escalated to SRE because retention compactor logs show compaction jobs touching org-specific partitions at the same time.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Log into console as a user in FluxHealth org.
2) Open dashboard 'Prod API Health' (shared id: dash-ff12a).
3) Set time range to 2026-03-08 20:00 UTC to 2026-03-09 05:00 UTC.
4) Add tag filter: route:/v1/generate.
5) Observe that series 'route:/v1/generate:userA' and 'route:/v1/generate:userB' are absent (panel shows 'No data').
6) Export panel CSV -> header includes series labels but the numeric columns for those series are empty.
7) Remove tag filter or expand time-range beyond retention window and series reappear.
logs:
Console retention compactor logs (console-prod-3):
[2026-03-09T02:04:21Z] compactor: start adaptive compaction job org=fluxhealth partition=2026-03-08-20
[2026-03-09T02:05:03Z] compactor: completed compaction org=fluxhealth partition=2026-03-08-20 removed_buckets=12
[2026-03-09T02:05:04Z] indexer: emit-rollup org=fluxhealth panel=dash-ff12a affected_series=[route:/v1/generate:userA, route:/v1/generate:userB]
[2026-03-09T02:05:07Z] storage: prune-sparse-buckets org=fluxhealth bucket=2026-03-08T20:00-20:05 retention_policy=adaptive-v2
Error traces from customer CSVs: attached_by_customer -> exported_csv_2026-03-09.csv (customer provided).
comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z - Aisha Khan (Support): Opened ticket after customer call. Attached CSV and screenshots; customer says trend lines disappeared at ~02:05 UTC and reappeared after removing tag filter.

2026-03-10T10:05:00Z - Marco Li (SRE): Triage: correlates with adaptive retention v2 rollout. Kicked off quick check against compactor logs and indexer metric. Asking for org-specific compaction job id and partition metrics.

2026-03-10T12:18:00Z - Julian Park (Platform): Initial hypothesis: pruning algorithm may be over-eager when tag cardinality is high and series density low. Added to reproduce queue. Requested sample query (provided by customer) and raw event IDs.

2026-03-11T08:23:00Z - Marco Li (SRE): Reproduced locally on staging by running compactor with same config; confirmed that rollup output omitted series where all bucket values fell below density threshold. Marking as regression from adaptive-retention:v2 change.
Linked PR for potential fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5840

2026-03-12T14:42:00Z - Aisha Khan (Support): Informed customer we identified root cause and applied a temporary workaround to their org (disabled adaptive pruning for affected partitions). Customer confirmed series visible again. Customer requested rollback notes and timeline for a permanent fix.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: adaptive retention's sparse-bucket pruning uses a density threshold that is applied post-filtering; when a dashboard applies a high-cardinality tag filter, buckets for specific series fall below threshold and are removed entirely rather than being replaced by rollup values.
Evidence:
- Local staging repro with same compactor config reproduces missing series.
- Compactor logs show 'removed_buckets' counters incremented for the exact partitions.
- Indexer emits rollup but storage prune happens after rollup and removes the series.
- Similar symptoms reported in SUP-703201 but that case was high-cardinality eviction after retention-eviction; this appears to be a separate codepath introduced in adaptive-v2.
Next steps:
- Revert pruning ordering so rollups are materialized before pruning for affected partitions (short term).
- Adjust density threshold/config to be org-aware or per-series (medium term).
- Add regression tests and dashboard-level sampling tests (long term).
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: disabled adaptive pruning for FluxHealth org on partitions 2026-03-08/2026-03-09. Verified dashboards render series and exported CSVs contain numeric values.
Temporary mitigation rolled out at 2026-03-12T13:50Z.
Permanent fix: engineering patch PR #5840 changes pruning ordering and adds safeguard to preserve series when tag filters are applied; targeted deploy to staging 2026-03-14 and canary to prod 2026-03-18.
Communications: CS notified customer; provided timeline and asked for acceptance testing window.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-Task: Backfill missing rollups for pruned partitions for FluxHealth (priority: high)
ENG-Task: Add unit/integration tests to simulate dashboard tag-filtering + adaptive-pruning combos
SRE-Task: Monitor compactor removed_buckets metric for 24h post-deploy and set alert threshold
DOC-Task: Update retention rollout runbook to include org-specific disable steps
